title: Two Piles, Same Weight
statement: You get a list of positive integers nums, the weights of some parcels. Return true if the parcels can be split into two piles of exactly equal total weight, with every parcel in exactly one pile, and false otherwise.

examples.why: The total is 10, so each pile needs 5: {3, 2} and {1, 1, 2, 1}.
{3, 3} and {2, 2, 2}. Dealing the heaviest parcel to the lighter pile ends at 7 against 5, so greedy says no.
The total 12 is even, but no group of parcels weighs exactly 6. An even total is not enough.

hints: If one pile weighs half of the total, the other pile does too. So the question is about one pile only.
Can some subset of the parcels sum to exactly total / 2? If the total is odd, the answer is no right away.
Keep a boolean array can[s] = some subset of the parcels seen so far sums to s. For each parcel x, update s from high to low: can[s] |= can[s − x].

explain.intuition:
Two equal piles means one pile weighs exactly total / 2; the rest automatically weighs the same. So this is subset sum: can some parcels hit the target T = total / 2? An odd total fails at once.

State: can[s] = some subset of the parcels processed so far sums to exactly s. Recurrence: after adding parcel x, a sum s is reachable if it already was (leave x out) or if s − x was (put x in): can[s] = can[s] || can[s − x]. Base: can[0] = true, the empty pile. Order: update s from T down to x. Going down means can[s − x] is still the value from before this parcel, so each parcel is used at most once. Going up would let one parcel be counted again and again. A bitset does the same update for all sums at once: bits |= bits << x.
steps: Compute the total. If it is odd, return false. Otherwise set T = total / 2.
State: can[s] = some subset of the parcels so far sums to s. Base: can[0] = true.
For each parcel x, for s from T down to x: can[s] = can[s] || can[s − x].
Return can[T] (you can stop early once it turns true).
pitfalls: Looping s upward. A single parcel then counts many times: [1, 2, 5] reaches 4 as 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 and wrongly returns true.
Returning true just because the total is even. [2, 2, 3, 5] is even and still impossible.
Greedy dealing, heaviest first into the lighter pile. The second example defeats it.

solutions.title: Try every subset
solutions.idea: For each parcel, put it in the target pile or leave it out, and check whether some choice hits total / 2.

solutions.title: Reachable sums, one row
solutions.idea: can[s] for every sum up to total / 2, updated from high to low so each parcel is used once.

solutions.title: Bitset of reachable sums
solutions.idea: Bit s is set when sum s is reachable. Adding parcel x shifts every reachable sum up by x at once.

followups: Split into k piles of equal weight instead of two. Why does this DP no longer suffice?
Return the smallest possible difference between the two piles instead of true or false.
Weights go up to 10⁹ but there are only 40 parcels. What would you do? (Hint: meet in the middle.)
